summary: The note surveys six initiatives launched from September 2023 onward that combine heritage recipes with sustainable cooking, in Malta, Tokyo, Scotland, Brazil, Rajasthan and France's Loire Valley. Each case pairs traditional dishes with local sourcing, biodiversity, or waste reduction to lower environmental impact while supporting farmers. The note concludes that sustainable food practices are a necessity for protecting both the planet and diverse cultures.
one_line: Six case studies from 2023 show chefs worldwide blending heritage recipes with sustainable, locally sourced, low-waste cooking practices.
key_facts: The Maltese Eco-Kitchen Initiative was launched in mid-September 2023 by a group of chefs led by culinary expert Francesca Zammit, using locally sourced ingredients to cut the carbon footprint of food transportation.
Zammit's team teaches small-scale Maltese farmers to grow indigenous crops organically, used in dishes such as "Stuffat tal-fenek" (rabbit stew) and "Pastizzi" (savory pastries).
Chef Kenjiro Hashimoto unveiled the "Zero-Waste Sushi Project" in Tokyo in the fall of 2023, using only sustainably farmed fish and turning every part of the fish, from skin to bones, into a dish.
Hashimoto's restaurant has also gone paperless, uses recycled chopsticks, and compacts food scraps for compost.
The Scottish Heirloom Garden was launched in early October 2023 by botanist Elaine McCallister to revive ancient Scottish grains and vegetables for recreating haggis.
The resulting "New Haggis" pairs sustainable meat with heirloom produce and is now served in restaurants across Scotland.
Chef Paulo de Oliveira launched the Rainforest Feast initiative in Brazil in November 2023, connecting indigenous growers with regional chefs in a forest-to-table supply chain.
Rainforest Feast uses only what the Amazon Rainforest can sustainably supply, including lesser-known fruits, nuts and plants, in dishes such as "Tacacá" and "Açaí na tigela".
Chef Aarav Singhania initiated a farm-to-fort movement in Rajasthan on September 15, 2023, with chefs and farmers growing pearl millet and cluster beans for dishes like "Ker Sangri" and "Bajra Roti".
Singhania's movement stresses organic farming that respects water scarcity in Rajasthan.
In September 2023 the French Family Farm Alliance, guided by agronomist Michel Giroux, began promoting ancient grain varieties in traditional French recipes among family farms in the Loire Valley.
Giroux's alliance encourages grain rotation to preserve soil health and ecosystem diversity, and restaurants use the grains in classics like "Coq au vin" and "Cassoulet".
